title: Development, Expansion, and In vivo Monitoring of Human NK Cells from Human Embryonic Stem Cells (hESCs) and Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells (iPSCs)
protocol: Dissociate hESCs or iPSCs using TrypLE.
Passage ES/iPS colonies no longer than 4-5 days before initiating the TrypLE passage.
Culture ES cells at a density to achieve ~70% confluence in 4 days.
Use regular ES media for culture of TrypLE-passaged ES cells.
Pass ES/iPS cells with collagenase IV four days prior to initiation of TrypLE passage.
Plate MEFs in 6-well plates at 0.9-1 x 10^5 cells/well one day before initiating the TrypLE passage.
Passage ES/iPS cells 1:1 in the first passage with TrypLE.
Expand ES/iPS cells accordingly beforehand for adaptation to TrypLE culture.
Pick off differentiated colonies carefully before proceeding to TrypLE dissociation.
Aspirate media from wells and add 1.0 ml pre-warmed TrypLE Select per well.
Incubate ES/iPS cells in TrypLE for 5 min at 37 °C.
Gently pipette ES cells off the bottom of the well after incubation.
Transfer the TrypLE cell suspension to a conical tube.
Pipette up and down gently 2-3 times to break apart clumps.
Dilute TrypLE with an equal volume of ES media and DPBS.
Spin down cells at 1,500 rpm for 5 min in a refrigerated centrifuge (8 °C).
Aspirate off as much of the supernatant as possible.
Resuspend cells in 4 ml ES media plus 4 ml DPBS.
Repeat spin to get rid of remaining traces of TrypLE.
Resuspend cells in appropriate volume ES media for plating.
Plate ES cells 1:1 (or 2:1 if necessary) onto low-density MEFs in ES media.
Feed cells with fresh ES media after 24 hours.
Feed ES cells daily with ES media.
Pass ES cells with TrypLE onto fresh MEFs every 3-4 days, typically on Tuesday and Friday.
Plate ES cells at a high density for the first 5-10 passages to ensure efficient plating efficiency.
Begin passing the cells at a ratio of 1:2 after passages 5-7 if they plate down efficiently enough to reach about 70% confluence within two days post-passage.
Increase the passaging ratio up to 1:4 as cell adaptation improves and differentiation is minimized.
Reconstitute 4 g of BSA in 35 ml IMDM.
Allow the BSA solution to sit at room temperature for 1-2 hours.
Adjust total volume to 40 ml with IMDM to achieve a final concentration of 10%.
Add approximately 1.3 g resin beads to 40 ml of BSA solution and shake well to mix.
Place the BSA solution (with resin beads) at 4°C until beads change color from blue-green to yellow.
Shake the solution every 20-30 minutes during exchange.
Centrifuge the solution for 2 minutes at 1,000 rpm after each exchange to pellet beads.
Pipette the BSA solution into a fresh 50 ml conical tube and discard the beads.
Repeat steps 2.2 through 2.5 at least two additional times for a total of three or more exchanges.
Sterile filter the BSA solution during the last exchange to remove any remaining beads.
The BSA solution should be stable at 4°C for at least 2 months.
Measure 100 ml Millipore H2O into a 125 ml glass bottle.
Add 5 g PVA to the water and mix thoroughly.
Place PVA/water solution at 4 °C overnight.
Incubate the PVA/water solution in a 37 °C water bath for 4-8 hours.
Return the bottle containing the PVA/water solution to 4 °C storage for an additional 24-48 hours or until fully dissolved.
Dilute Linoleic and Linolenic Acids to 1 mg/ml in 200-proof ethanol by adding 10 ml of pure oil to 10 ml of ethanol.
Aliquot the diluted linoleic and linolenic acid solutions and store at -20°C.
Dilute 13 μl of α-MTG in 1 ml IMDM to prepare an α-MTG stock solution.
Prepare a 5 mg/ml Ascorbic Acid 2-Phosphate solution by dissolving 250 mg ascorbic acid 2-phosphate in 50 ml sterile, tissue-culture grade H2O.
Add 20 ml IMDM and 20 ml F-12 nutrient mixture to a 50 ml conical tube.
Add 10 ml of 5% PVA stock, 0.4 ml synthechol, 20 μl linolenic acid, and 20 μl linoleic acid for 200 ml BPEL media preparation.
Shake the mixture well to ensure thorough mixing.
Add all remaining media components to the top of a 250 ml Stericup filtration unit.
Mix the PVA-lipids mixture from step 1 and add it to the top of the Stericup.
Filter the medium.
Aspirate culture media off of ES/iPS cells.
Add 1.0 ml pre-warmed TrypLE Select to each well containing ES/iPS cells.
Place plates in incubator at 37 °C for 5 min.
Gently pipette cells off of the plate.
Collect dissociated cells in a conical tube.
Pipette up and down to break apart clumps.
Dilute TrypLE with 1 equal volume of BPEL media and at least 1 equal volume of DPBS.
Remove supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 5 ml BPEL media plus 5 ml DPBS.
Repeat spin.
Remove supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 5-10 ml BPEL media, depending on anticipated cell number.
Pass cells through a 70 μm filter into a fresh 50 ml conical tube to remove clumps.
Count filtered cells.
Aliquot cells for plating into a 50 ml conical and spin.
Resuspend cells to 3x10^4 cells/ml after centrifugation.
Prepare a volume of BPEL media + cytokines sufficient for resuspending the cells (6 ml/plate).
Mix cells by pipetting before use.
Plate 100 μl of cells/well (=3,000 cells/well) into each of the inner 60 wells of the prepared 96-well plates.
Spin the 96-well plates in a refrigerated centrifuge for 4 min at ~1,500 rpm, 8 °C.
Transfer the plates carefully from the centrifuge to a 37 °C incubator.
Check the plates to ensure that cells formed uniform pellets in the bottom of the wells.
Do not feed or disturb stage I spin EBs between days 3-4 until they have developed a more durable outer layer.
If left beyond 10-12 days, sometimes feed EBs with 50 μl fresh BPEL media with cytokines by first removing 50 μl of old media from each well.
Within 24 hours, cells should start forming a 3-D EB structure and develop a distinct outer layer by day 3-5, beginning to form cystic structures.
Collect around 18-36 spin EBs for FACS analysis if analyzing before day 6, requiring more wells to obtain sufficient cell numbers.
Prepare the necessary volume of trypsin with 2% chicken serum and place in a 37 °C water bath until use.
Transfer spin EBs and media from 96-well plates to 15 ml conical tubes.
Allow EBs to settle to the bottom of conical tubes.
Carefully pipette out the supernatant with a 5 ml pipette and transfer it to a separate tube.
Resuspend EBs in trypsin + 2% chicken serum: use 3-4 ml for each 15 ml conical tube.
Place the EBs with trypsin in a 37 °C water bath for 3-7 minutes.
Shake or gently vortex every 1-2 minutes during incubation.
Quench trypsin by adding at least one equal volume of FBS-containing media.
Spin down cells at 1,500 rpm for 5 minutes at 8 °C.
Resuspend cells in an appropriate volume of media for counting (usually 3-5 ml).
Filter cells through a 100 μm cell strainer.
Remove an aliquot of cells for counting.
Transfer 6 spin EBs to each well of a 24-well plate using a multichannel pipette set to 100 μl.
If using feeders, transfer spin EBs to wells containing 100,000 irradiated EL08-1D2 cells per well.
Without feeders, transfer EBs directly to uncoated 24-well plates.
Add 400 μl of NK differentiation media containing cytokines (IL-3, IL-15, IL-7, SCF, Flt3L) to each well to make the total volume ~1 ml.
Feed cells every 5-7 days with NK differentiation media containing all cytokines except IL-3.
Irradiate mice with 225-250 cGY 24 hours prior to tumor cell injection.
Resuspend 1 x 10^6 K562 cells in 200 μl of IMDM supplemented with 20% FBS.
Inject the resuspended cells subcutaneously into the upper left thorax of mice using a 27 or 28 gauge needle.
Allow the injected cells to engraft for 4 days.
Resuspend hESC-derived NK cells (10 x 10^6 NK cells) in 300 μl of IMDM supplemented with 20% FBS without antibiotics.
Inject the resuspended NK cells into each mouse intraperitoneally using a 27 or 28 gauge needle.
Give mice a 250 μl IP injection of IL-2 (1x104 U/mouse) and IL-15 (10 ng/mouse) in sterile DPBS every day for the first 7 days followed by IL-2 only every 2 to 3 days until the time of sacrifice.
Monitor engraftment of hESC-derived NK cells by bioluminescent imaging.
Inject each mouse IP with 120 μl D-luciferin (150 mg/kg).
Image the mice 10 min after D-luciferin injection.
Anesthetize mice using a chamber allowing isoflurane entry into the box at 0.8 l/min.
Place anesthetized mice in IVIS Spectrum and secure mice on their backs using tape or Velcro.
Set IVIS machine to correct imaging platform (D for 4-5 mice, C for 3 or fewer mice).
Set binning to medium, f/stop to 1 and acquire image for 1 min.
Use the imaging wizard to set up an emission scan measuring the probe of interest as well as background signal.
Choose Input Em/Ex from the list of probes.
Enter correct excitation and emission values for turboFP650 (excitation: 605 nm, emission: 660-720 nm).
Measure tumor signal using auto exposure settings.
Select the desired imaging platform.
Use correct excitation and emission values for background signal measurement (excitation: 570 nm, emission: 640-720 nm).
Allow mice to fully recover from anesthesia before transporting from the imaging system.
Analyze images using Living Image software package version 4.2 (Caliper Life Sciences).
Quantify bioluminescent signal using a region of interest set to total flux or average radiance and set all images to the same scale.
Use representative images to demonstrate both cell populations in each mouse.
Optimize colocalization timing based on the experimental model used.
To quantify fluorescent signal from the emission scan sequence, use the "Spectral Unmixing" feature in Living Image.
Select the images to include in the analysis and draw a mask over the area of the mouse containing the signal of interest.
Select tissue autofluorescence and unknown probe to be unmixed.
If mice are given food containing alfalfa, unmix food signal from the probe of interest and tissue autofluorescence.
Set a high pass filter for 640 nm under the update tab for consistent tissue autofluorescence distribution and better signal separation.
Quantify fluorescent signal from the unmixed image using a region of interest set to radiant efficiency (photons/sec/cm2/sr)/μW) and set all images to the same scale.
Sacrifice mice at a desired time point for analysis of engraftment of hESC-derived cells by flow cytometry.
Analyze peripheral blood, spleen, and peritoneum for intraperitoneally injected NK cells.
Expose just the peritoneal membrane and make a medial incision wide enough to allow access with a glass Pasteur pipette.
Use sterile PBS to perform several washes of the peritoneal cavity by rotating the mouse thoroughly.
Collect sufficient fluid until you have a visible pellet following centrifugation (typically 5-10 ml of wash).
